page: Amazon Web Services t2.small is an entry-level burstable instance managed under the Xen hypervisor within the General Purpose family. It provides 1 vCPU mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 core operating at 2.5 GHz on the i386 architecture, paired with 2.0 GB of system memory and 45 MB of L3 cache. The CPU configuration provides basic vector instruction support such as AVX, AES, and BMI2, while omitting newer extensions like AVX-512 and AMX. This instance type contains 0 GPUs, does not bundle any local storage, and features a baseline network bandwidth rating of 0 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place the t2.small instance in the lower percentiles across compute and memory operations. In synthetic processor evaluations, it achieved a stress-ng score of 855.28, a PassMark CPU score of 1442.32, a Geekbench single-core score of 850.0, and a Geekbench multi-core score of 852.0. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reached 9.8 GB/sec with write throughput at 6.99 GB/sec. In application-focused metrics, the system handled 0.5 million Redis SET operations per second and delivered 1.09 GB/sec of static web serving throughput. Sustained intensive compute is limited by the burstable CPU credit mechanism, which throttles output to baseline capacity when CPU credits are depleted.

Qualitatively, t2.small provides an economical compute footprint for low-intensity workloads that do not require continuous full-core execution. Because local storage is absent, instances rely completely on network-attached block storage. The constrained 2.0 GB memory capacity also restricts the deployment of memory-dense services. The instance is technically appropriate for low-traffic web serving, basic background utilities, small CI/CD workers, development testbeds, and lightweight monitoring daemons.
